panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels ((a), (b), (c)). (a): Gross autopsy specimen of a human liver with diffuse dark-red congestion and documented enlargement beyond normal range for age, attributed in a Sanfilippo syndrome autopsy article to systemic lysosomal storage; hepatosplenomegaly is a listed MPS III finding. (b): Gross specimen of an enlarged, congestive human spleen with weight above normal range for age, captioned in an MPS III autopsy report as indicating systemic lysosomal storage disease. (c): Gross autopsy specimen of a human kidney with dark cortical discoloration and congestive parenchyma, overweight for age, described as part of systemic lysosomal storage in the MPS III autopsy; kidney congestion is not itself a specific listed MPS III finding, so hepatosplenomegaly is used as the closest vocabulary key with a lower confidence.
